title: Indexing and coefficient isomorphism of a supported degree family
statement:
Let $n,s,t\in\mathbf N$, let $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_s\in\mathbf N^n$ be distinct coordinatewise incomparable vectors in any fixed order, and put $D=\bigcup_i(\alpha_i+\mathbf N^n)$, $d_i=|\alpha_i|$, $\Delta_i=\{\beta:\alpha_i+\beta\notin\bigcup_{h<i}(\alpha_h+\mathbf N^n)\}$. Here $|\eta|=\sum_j\eta_j$. Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $H_i\in A[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]$ be homogeneous of degrees $d_i$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and write $V_t$ for the degree-$t$ homogeneous submodule. With the supported division conventions [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division], set
$$I_t=\{(i,\beta):\beta\in\Delta_i,\ |\beta|+d_i=t\}\amalg\{\gamma\notin D:|\gamma|=t\},\quad E_t=\{\eta\in\mathbf N^n:|\eta|=t\}.$$
These are finite sets, and the map $\theta_t:I_t\to E_t$ sending $(i,\beta)$ to $\alpha_i+\beta$ and a remainder index $\gamma$ to $\gamma$ is a bijection. Its inverse sends an exponent in $D$ to its first dividing vertex and the difference exponent. The monomials $(Y^\eta)_{\eta\in E_t}$ form an $A$-basis of $V_t$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Define $P_{(i,\beta)}=Y^\beta H_i$ and $P_\gamma=Y^\gamma$. Let $T_t:A^{E_t}\to A^{E_t}$ be the linear map whose column at $\eta$ is the monomial coefficient vector of $P_{\theta_t^{-1}(\eta)}$. Then the indexed family $(P_\xi)_{\xi\in I_t}$ spans $V_t$ if and only if $T_t$ is surjective; whenever this holds $T_t$ is bijective and $(P_\xi)$ is an $A$-basis of $V_t$. All assertions include $n=0$, $s=0$, and the zero ring.

proof.text: For $\eta\in E_t\cap D$, choose the least $i$ such that $\alpha_i\le\eta$ coordinatewise and put $\beta=\eta-\alpha_i$. Then $\alpha_i+\beta=\eta$, $|\beta|+d_i=t$, and no earlier vertex divides $\eta$, so $\beta\in\Delta_i$. If $\eta\notin D$, choose its remainder index. Conversely, a pair $(i,\beta)\in I_t$ has $\alpha_i+\beta\in D$ and $i$ as its least dividing vertex, while a remainder index has image outside $D$. Thus these recipes are inverse to $\theta_t$. Each coordinate of an element of $E_t$ is at most $t$, so $E_t$ is a subset of the finite set $\{0,\ldots,t\}^n$. Its bijection with $I_t$ proves finiteness of both.

source.place: Agent coefficient calculation from the polynomial and supported-family definitions; finite-module input: Tag 05G8, lemma-fun.

proof.text: By the polynomial-ring definition a polynomial is a unique finite coefficient family on exponent vectors. A homogeneous degree-$t$ polynomial is exactly such a family vanishing outside $E_t$. Therefore the mutually inverse linear maps are $C:V_t\to A^{E_t}$, $C(f)_\eta=\operatorname{coeff}_\eta(f)$, and $B:A^{E_t}\to V_t$, $B(c)=\sum_{\eta\in E_t}c_\eta Y^\eta$. Indeed coefficient extraction gives $C(B(c))=c$, and the unique monomial expansion gives $B(C(f))=f$. This proves the claimed monomial basis by the definition of basis.

source.place: Agent coefficient calculation from the polynomial and supported-family definitions; finite-module input: Tag 05G8, lemma-fun.

proof.text: Each $P_\xi$ lies in $V_t$: for a pair index expand $H_i=\sum_{|\mu|=d_i}h_{i\mu}Y^\mu$. Multiplication by $Y^\beta$ gives $\sum_{|\mu|=d_i}h_{i\mu}Y^{\beta+\mu}$, and every exponent has degree $|\beta|+d_i=t$. A remainder monomial already has degree $t$. Consequently $S:A^{I_t}\to V_t$, $S(a)=\sum_{\xi\in I_t}a_\xi P_\xi$, is a well-defined linear map. No leading-coefficient condition on $H_i$ is used.

source.place: Agent coefficient calculation from the polynomial and supported-family definitions; finite-module input: Tag 05G8, lemma-fun.

proof.text: Let $R_\theta:A^{E_t}\to A^{I_t}$ send $c$ to $(c_{\theta_t(\xi)})_\xi$; its inverse sends $a$ to $(a_{\theta_t^{-1}(\eta)})_\eta$. For every $c$ and $\mu\in E_t$, the column definition gives $(T_t c)_\mu=\sum_{\eta\in E_t}c_\eta\operatorname{coeff}_\mu(P_{\theta_t^{-1}(\eta)})=(C S R_\theta(c))_\mu$. Thus $T_t=C S R_\theta$. The image of $S$ consists precisely of the finite linear combinations of the indexed family, since $I_t$ is finite. By the supported-family definition, spanning $V_t$ is therefore equivalent to surjectivity of $S$, and hence of $T_t$, since $C$ and $R_\theta$ are bijective.

source.place: Agent coefficient calculation from the polynomial and supported-family definitions; finite-module input: Tag 05G8, lemma-fun.

proof.text: Assume this spanning condition. The coordinate unit vectors $e_\eta$ generate $A^{E_t}$: every $c$ equals $\sum_{\eta\in E_t}c_\eta e_\eta$. Thus $A^{E_t}$ is a finitely generated module over the given commutative ring $A$, and $T_t$ is its surjective linear endomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-surjective-endomorphism-bijective] (Stacks Tag 05G8, lemma-fun) to conclude that $T_t$ is an isomorphism, in particular bijective.

source.place: Agent coefficient calculation from the polynomial and supported-family definitions; finite-module input: Tag 05G8, lemma-fun.

proof.text: The identity $T_t=C S R_\theta$ now makes $S=C^{-1}T_tR_\theta^{-1}$ bijective. Hence every $f\in V_t$ has a unique coefficient family $a\in A^{I_t}$ with $f=\sum_\xi a_\xi P_\xi$; finiteness of $I_t$ makes these precisely the finite coefficients in the definition of a basis. This proves that $(P_\xi)$ is an $A$-basis. The argument also covers the boundary cases: when $s=0$ every index is a remainder; when $n=0$, $E_0$ is the singleton empty exponent and $E_t$ is empty for $t>0$; over the zero ring every coefficient module is the zero module and the same inverse formulas and finite-module lemma apply.
